protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; records permission-truth-tables.v2 as DR-105's accepted design-contract candidate
summary: Every digest recital in the entry reproduces exactly, including my own verdict at 021bacaf and its characterization as ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES 0 blockers 3 SHOULD-FIX, which is precisely what I returned. The four named attacks fail: SATISFIED appears twice and both are refusals, host acts are explicitly not made exercisable, file 08 is untouched in git and matches the recited digest, and the advisories are neither erased nor treated as blockers. One SHOULD-FIX blocks CONSENT. The entry invokes the D-013/D-015/D-035/D-038 recording form, and every one of those four precedents names what remains unmet on the row it records. D-042 says only 'DR-105 stays OPEN' and never names the remaining halves. The omission that matters most is the DR-105/DR-114 join: adopted D-032 left BLK-1/2/3/4 STILL-ROUTED, adopted D-038 carried a dedicated clause saying so while recording the other half of that same join, and D-042 -- recording the permission half -- contains zero occurrences of BLK, join, or FC-C1.

objections.location: Decision clause 3, and the decision-type line's 'Same form as D-035 / D-038'
objections.claim: The entry claims a recording form whose defining feature it omits. Every cited precedent names what remains unmet on the recorded row; D-042 names nothing, and the unnamed items include four join blockers that are STILL-ROUTED by adopted decision.
evidence: D-042 clause 3 reads in full: 'DR-105 stays `OPEN`. No `SATISFIED`. Host-under-instruction remains outside this vocabulary (D-032). This recording does not make any host or component act exercisable.' No remaining work is named.

D-038, cited by name as the same form, carries clause 4: 'Join blockers BLK-1/2/3/4 remain STILL-ROUTED. This entry discharges none of them.' D-038 was recording host-effect-authorization.v8 -- the other half of the same DR-105/DR-114 join.
D-035, also cited by name, states 'The row stays `OPEN`: actor-scope and fixture execution unmet.'

The live file-08 DR-105 status cell states 'Join with doctor v1 remains **INCOHERENT at 7 blockers** (538f3681…)' and 'D-032 dispositions that join; a permission v2 successor and the host-effect contract remain.'
The live DR-114 status cell uses the same discipline: 'the actor-join and fixture-execution halves remain open.'
Adopted D-032 records the per-blocker standing: BLK-1/2/3/4 STILL-ROUTED, BLK-5 DISCHARGED, BLK-6 DISCHARGED-AS-INAPPLICABLE for host, BLK-7 REPAIRED-IN-V4. Four of the seven remain live.
grep over the D-042 draft for BLK, join, FC-C1, and implementation returns zero matches.
objections.whyItMatters: D-042 is the entry that records the permission half of an INCOHERENT join. That is the moment at which a reader is most likely to conclude the join is progressing toward coherence, and it is the moment the precedent form exists to guard. D-038 guarded it explicitly when recording the other half. Reading D-042 alone, a reader learns that DR-105 has an accepted design-contract candidate and that the row is OPEN, but not that four join blockers are STILL-ROUTED, not that FC-C1 still requires an owner-recorded live instance, and not that fixture execution remains. Clause 3's 'does not make any host or component act exercisable' preserves the operative safety property, which is why this is a SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker -- but it states the effect while omitting the reasons, and the reasons are what the next entry has to pick up.
objections.remedy: Add a clause in the D-038 form: name BLK-1/2/3/4 as STILL-ROUTED and discharged by nothing here, name FC-C1 as still requiring the owners' live instance, and name what else DR-105 still owes (acceptance-evidence execution). Adding 'No `docs/v2/implementation/`' would complete the parallel with D-038 clause 3.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: f974b2f82bcb53b092c84c714601a17a4a06da709242b2154148c6a53cf1e749 both times, matching the dispatch's recital. No drift.

The attack 'verdicts were not 0-blocker' fails on my half, and I can state this from my own bytes rather than from the entry's account. The entry pins Claude 2 at 021bacaf071dfa682e3e85574f42306adc3f2b12607e0bbd94b01aa344389301; I measured my verdict file and it is exactly that. It characterizes it as 'ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES 0 blockers, 3 SHOULD-FIX'; my file carries verdict ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, mustFix 0, shouldFix 3. Exact on all three counts.

The Codex verdict digest is correct at c32f98751b848e3d2ccbe6e9927e60ea8e640f0b655315ebd1fc295c5a1e856d, confirmed by hashing that file without opening it. It is the same file I hashed during the permission v2 review, so the pin is stable across dispatches.
The subject pin is correct: permission-truth-tables.v2.json at cce3afcaee90bbca388825a474751d6ebb17b30722b35dadcf6c631b34a8731a, matching my own measurement of that artifact in both dispatches.

The environment pins are correct AND current, which is stronger than correct: COORD at a4d497383ef26f7be1a0072ca260d1776ec5f4ba525444eaeb1ea16d4d527f6a and file 08 at 877e36d3b597fb9b51c1c91fb6b6c6f27eabdcb8b2b1a941ade2b34850a0f58f both match live bytes. A re-measurement clause is present.
No silent SATISFIED. Two occurrences, both refusals: clause 3's 'No `SATISFIED`' and the rejected alternative 'Mark SATISFIED. Rejected.' DR-105 is stated OPEN.

Host acts are not made exercisable. Clause 3 states 'This recording does not make any host or component act exercisable' and preserves D-032's placement of host-under-instruction outside the vocabulary. I checked this against adopted D-032's own text, which requires a scoped host-effect authorization contract as 'necessary, not sufficient' before CA-1 host head, CA-2, CA-3 or host CA-4 is exercisable, fail-closed until then. Nothing in D-042 disturbs that.
File 08 is not edited. Clause 4 states 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6)', git reports the file unmodified, and its live digest matches the recital. Same for COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md.

Advisories are neither erased nor treated as blockers. Clause 2 names all four -- P2-01, P2-02, P2-03, PT2-CX-A1 -- states they are not blockers, and states they 'remain owed as honesty work on a successor, not as a reason to withhold the recording'. My three ids are exactly P2-01, P2-02 and P2-03, so the enumeration of my half is complete and none of mine was dropped. This is the correct disposition and it is the one I would have asked for.

The decision-type line does not repeat the defect I raised against D-039 turn 1. It says 'Records independent ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES (0 blockers from both reviewers)' rather than calling an ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES an ACCEPT. The verdict class is stated accurately for my half.

'0 blockers is the D-035 gate' is accurate. D-035's adopted status line reads 'RULE-GOVERNED recording of an independent ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES (0 blockers)', so the precedent for recording on a 0-blocker ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES with live advisories is real and correctly cited.

The word 'candidate' in clause 1 is more conservative than the precedents, not less. D-035 and D-038 record 'the accepted design contract'; D-042 records 'DR-105's accepted design-contract candidate', which matches the artifact's own status of CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED. Examined and declined as a finding -- it is a tightening.
The entry is single-subject and severable: 'Subject: docs/coop/artifacts/permission-truth-tables.v2.json only.' No bundling with the section31 subject reviewed alongside it.

My P2-01 and P2-02 concerned the recorded artifact carrying a stale copy of its own register row. I checked whether recording it could propagate that staleness into the register, and it cannot: clause 4 does not edit file 08, so file 08 remains the authority on DR-105's standing. Examined and declined.

Whether the DR-105 owners (Security + platform) will act on this recording.

I carry those limits forward rather than letting this recording imply broader coverage: in particular I did not re-derive the four CARRIED v1 advisories, and I opened only FX-2B and FX-6 of the thirteen fixture classes.

Whether BLK-1/2/3/4 have been discharged by anything after D-038. I searched COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md for BLK and STILL-ROUTED and found the standing set by D-032 and re-affirmed by D-038, with no later discharge. I did not audit every adopted entry individually for an implicit discharge.

nonConsentNote: I do not CONSENT, on one SHOULD-FIX, and I want the narrowness of that on the record. The recording itself is well-founded: the gate is real, the precedent is correctly cited, the verdict recitals reproduce against my own bytes, and the four attacks the dispatch named all fail. My objection is to an omission rather than an assertion -- nothing D-042 says is false. But the entry claims a form whose defining move is naming what remains, makes that claim while recording one half of a join that adopted D-032 left STILL-ROUTED at four blockers, and the sibling entry recording the other half of that same join carried the clause D-042 drops. One clause repairs it.
